blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A ReportStore interface has load, list, save and purge. The dashboard calls load and list, the importer calls save, and the retention job calls list and purge. A read-only ArchiveStore implements ReportStore today and throws from save and purge. Which design removes those throwing methods without making any client take two parameters or an intersection type?

options.text: Three interfaces, ReportReader (load, list), ReportWriter (save, purge) and ReportStore extending both, since the archive implements only ReportReader
options.says: roles follow what clients use together; the dashboard takes the reader, the importer the writer, the retention job the store, and the archive can't be handed to the job

options.text: Three interfaces, ReportReader (load, list), ReportWriter (save) and ReportPurger (purge), since the archive implements only ReportReader
options.says: the retention job calls list and purge, so it would need ReportReader and ReportPurger together: two parameters or an intersection type

options.text: Four interfaces, one per method, since the archive then implements only the two it supports and every client picks the ones it calls
options.says: with one interface per method the dashboard and the retention job each need two of them, which means an intersection type or several fields holding one object

options.text: One interface plus an isWritable() method, since the archive then answers false and every client checks it before it saves or purges
options.says: the archive still has save and purge to stub, and a caller that forgets the check fails at run time exactly as before

origin.section: Role Interfaces Turn the Refusal into a Compile Error

questions.stem: A NotificationSender interface has send, sendBulk and cancel. One production class implements it, and fifteen test fakes implement it for services that only ever call send. A team adds an abstract method status(String id) and implements it in the production class. What happens when the whole codebase is rebuilt?

options.text: It builds, since a fake is checked only for the methods its service calls, which excludes status()
options.says: javac checks that every non-abstract class implementing the interface implements all its abstract methods, whoever calls them

options.text: It builds, since the fakes are compiled as test sources, apart from the interface they implement
options.says: test sources are compiled against the same interface; on the page the test fake failed to compile

options.text: It fails, since each fake now lacks status(), a method the service it stands in for never calls
options.says: an abstract method added to a fat interface breaks every implementation, including fakes for services that never call it

options.text: It fails, since each service that uses a fake now lacks a call to status(), a method it never needed
options.says: callers that don't use the new method compile unchanged; it is the implementing classes, here the fakes, that break

origin.section: A Method Added to a Fat Interface Breaks Classes That Never Call It

questions.stem: GuardedQueue, written in 2012, extends AbstractCollection and declares add, remove, size and iterator; add, remove and size are synchronized methods. A new cleanup task calls queue.removeIf(job -> job.expired()) while worker threads keep calling add. What does removeIf do?

options.text: It runs under the queue's lock, since removeIf calls the synchronized size() before it walks iterator()
options.says: removeIf is Collection's default; it calls iterator() and Iterator.remove() and never takes the queue's lock

options.text: It runs under the queue's lock, since inherited methods share the lock of the class's synchronized ones
options.says: synchronized applies only to the methods declared with it; the inherited default takes no lock

options.text: It runs outside the queue's lock, since it walks and deletes through iterator() and Iterator.remove() alone
options.says: the inherited default iterates without the lock, so a worker's add can land mid-iteration; the class must override removeIf to keep its locking

options.text: It runs outside the queue's lock, since the class predates removeIf and gets a default that throws
options.says: Collection.removeIf has a working default that iterates and removes; it doesn't throw by default

origin.section: A Default Method Keeps Implementations Compiling, and Runs Code That Never Saw Their Locks

questions.stem: ChapterList, a read-only class, extends AbstractCollection<Chapter> and implements SequencedCollection<Chapter>, overriding only iterator(), size() and reversed(). An editor screen holds one as a SequencedCollection<Chapter> and calls addLast(appendix). What happens?

options.text: It fails to compile, since the interface's own addLast is abstract and ChapterList declares none
options.says: addLast has a default body in SequencedCollection, inherited by every implementation, so the call compiles

options.text: It fails at run time with UnsupportedOperationException, since the interface's own addLast refuses the call
options.says: SequencedCollection's default addLast always throws UnsupportedOperationException; javac accepts the call and the read-only class refuses it at run time

options.text: It appends the chapter, since the interface's own addLast falls back on the collection's add()
options.says: the default addLast doesn't call add(); it throws UnsupportedOperationException

options.text: It appends the chapter, since the interface's own addLast writes through the collection's iterator()
options.says: no default writes through the iterator for addLast; it throws, and only removeFirst/removeLast use the iterator

origin.section: Collection Is Fat on Purpose, and Java 21's SequencedCollection Repeats It

concepts: An abstract method added to a fat interface breaks every implementation, test fakes for clients that never call it included; a new role breaks nobody.

A read-only implementation of a JDK collection interface, Java 21's SequencedCollection included, compiles calls to the mutators it offers and refuses them at run time, since no read-only role exists to implement instead.
A role is the set of methods one client uses together; one interface per method makes a client that needs several carry an intersection type.
